ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (No. 13 of 1987), as amended; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, as amended; Terrorism Financing Prevention Act 2012; Beneficial Ownership Regulations 2019; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2019; and the Samoa Companies Act 2001, administered with the AML/CFT Consolidated Supervision Guidelines of the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (i.e. UBO information is held by the licensed Samoa registered agent and shared with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, the Tax Administration and the Registrar upon lawful demand; the general public has no access and nominee shareholders/registered agents are lawfully available).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the applicant's country of residence or competent consular/embassy authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the source country is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise full consular legalization through the Samoan consulate or Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or recent bank statement) for each UBO, director and shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution plus notary public recognition
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in accordance with source-country practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter confirming the beneficial owner's banking relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Overseas issuing bank signed by a bank officer, then notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; the Samoa registered agent may accept a bank-confirmed SWIFT/courier original only after direct verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional reference / CV statement of integrity for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed lawyer, certified accountant or recognized compliance professional
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization to establish genuineness of signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract of foreign corporate register and incumbency certificate when the shareholder or director is a legal person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry (Registrar of Companies) or licensed corporate services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or consular-legalized certificate, accompanied by certified English translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, officer, connected family member and close associate must be screened against the following mandatory lists before onboarding: United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; OFAC SDN/SSI list; European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; United Kingdom OFSI list; Australia DFAT consolidated list; Samoa domestic AML/CFT enforcement and suspicious activity lists; and recognized PEP databases. In addition, a real-time adverse-media check and politically exposed person (PEP) assessment must be prepared. Any PEP designation or sanctions hit automatically triggers enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, source-of-wealth documentation and, if necessary, rejection of the engagement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies and International Trusts Registry – International Companies Online Name Search and Name Reservation Portal (administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL))
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be in Roman/Latin script. A name using Chinese or any non-Roman script will be accepted only if a standard romanized transliteration and certified English translation is submitted; the Registrar will keep the romanized version as the official name. The name must not, in the Registrar's opinion, be identical or confusingly similar to a registered name or a protected government eminence, and must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc.' or an equivalent recognized suffix. Chinese-language articles and memorandum may be authorized by the directors, but an official English version remains the controlling document filed with the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar within 14 calendar days, using the prescribed appeal form and attaching the official rejection notice, a revised constitutional document, and any consent letters for sensitive tokens. The Registrar must issue a reasoned decision within 10 working days. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may within 30 days apply to the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review. A rejected name may be re-submitted with modifications without prejudice, but a fresh reservation fee and a new 30-day reservation period will apply.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A strictly virtual head office is not sufficient for an International Company. The company must maintain a physical, public-accessible registered office in Samoa at the address of its licensed registered agent, where statutory records, registers of directors/shareholders and UBO files are kept. Operational activities, app publishing, customer support and payment-rail contracting may be conducted entirely from outside Samoa without creating a taxable or commercial presence in Samoa. A virtual office or mail-forwarding address may be used for correspondence only, provided the Samoa physical registered office remains effective.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate; approximate annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection is 5-10% for a medium-risk AML/CFT-tiered international company in the app and simulated gaming sector. The likelihood falls to 2-4% if the registered agent has a clean supervisory record and the company maintains complete registers. A suspicious transaction report, sanctions hit or adverse media event raises the probability to high and triggers immediate inspection by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit or Registrar.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 6 (incorporation), 12 (registered office), 16 (memorandum and articles), 30 (shares) and 67 (officers); read with the International Companies Regulations 1988.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), in coordination with the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation of an International Company together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Samoa International Company; one ordinary share subscribed by the sole subscriber is sufficient. No escrow or capital deposit account is required for this non-banking, non-captive software activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company be and is hereby ratified; that the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed with the Registrar of International Companies be adopted; and that the subscription of one ordinary share by the initial subscriber be approved and allotted to sole member. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office situated at Level 2, SIFA Centre, Apia, Samoa, be and is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory registered office and address for service. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Director Name] be appointed as sole Director, and that [Secretary Name] be appointed as Company Secretary. All officers are authorized to execute bank account openings, payment rails agreements (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing), and any filings incidental to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) via the Samoa eRegistry online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application for reservation of the proposed corporate name. The name must be in English or a vernacular equivalent, must not be obscene or identical to an existing registered company name, and must not imply a prohibited activity. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee by wire transfer or EFTPOS. A successful reservation is valid for 90 days, during which the incorporation filings must be completed.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Certified copy of the subscriber's passport
Registered agent consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on distinctiveness or public interest grounds, file a fresh application with an alternative name or submit a written administrative review request to the Registrar within 14 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SIFA Compliance and Beneficial Ownership Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA), AML/CFT Compliance Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the CDD pack through the licensed registered agent for the International Company. Provide certified passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owner, a professional or bank reference, and a declaration of source of funds. This pre-clearance ensures the entity meets the fit-and-proper and know-your-customer standards of SIFA before incorporation is endorsed.
required_dossiers: SIFA CDD Self-Verification Form (IC-CDD)
Certified passport copy of the ultimate beneficial owner
Bank or legal professional reference letter
Source of funds and source of wealth declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA raises verification queries, respond through the registered agent within 10 business days with supplemental evidence; if the response is inadequate, SIFA may refuse endorsement, and the applicant may resubmit after curing the identified due diligence gaps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Subscriber before a Notary Public in Samoa or a witness permitted under the International Companies Act 1987.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscriber executes the Memorandum and Articles of Association in a single counterpart, subscribing to at least one share. Appoint the licensed registered agent and adopt the registered office address at SIFA Centre, Apia. Include standard clauses covering object purposes, share structure, director powers, and indemnity.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (printed counterpart)
Registered Agent Appointment Form
Consent to Act as Director
Consent to Act as Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial or witness attestation is defective, re-execute the relevant signature block with a correct jurat; no registry penalty is imposed if the corrected instrument is refiled before formal lodgement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, consent letters, notice of registered office and registered agent, and pay the USD 250 incorporation fee. Upon satisfaction, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the company becomes a body corporate with limited liability.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent
Consents of initial Director and Company Secretary
Statement of Compliance from the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of defective filing, the applicant has 30 days to supply the missing information or pay any corrective fee; failure to cure may result in the application being treated as withdrawn, with government fees refunded except the administrative component.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Revenue (SMoR) and the Registrar of International Companies, MCIL.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to ratify the incorporation, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, and open corporate bank accounts. Apply for a tax identification certificate confirming the International Company's tax-exempt status, and file the first annual return for the year of incorporation. Execute Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant agreements using the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Minutes of the First Board Meeting
Application for tax-exempt status confirmation
Evidence of registered office (lease or agent consent)
Director and officer identification records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax-exempt confirmation is delayed, rely on the statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 1987 and provide a legal opinion letter from counsel to payment processors and partner banks to evidence the exempt status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a digital software publisher; if an Apia office lease is executed, building occupancy approval is obtained from the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) under the Samoa Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No government operating licence is required. Simulated social casino and virtual slots software is non-real-money entertainment and falls outside the Samoa Gambling Act 1976 licensing regime; Apple App Store and Google Play require only platform merchant agreements, not a state gaming permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - administrative office use only; no mandatory EIA Report for a software publishing business occupying less than 500 m2 of office floor area; only waste disposal registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to wastewater or VOC emissions for code-only operations. Office sanitary effluent must connect to the Samoa Water Authority (SWA) sewer system or approved septic tank; electronic hardware waste must be consigned to a registered waste handler under the Waste Management Act regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for the registered office; compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 covering workspace ventilation, electrical safety, and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa (official online portal: 'Samoa Ministry of Revenue – Online Services / Aso Avanoa')
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities incorporated as Samoa International Companies (ICs) obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN) from the Ministry for Revenue as part of the registration process administered through the Registrar of International Companies within the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA). For VAGST purposes, a non-resident IC that carries on a taxable activity in Samoa (or makes taxable supplies such as digital gaming services to Samoan consumers) must register for VAGST using Form VAGST-REG through the Ministry for Revenue online portal. If the entity undertakes exclusively offshore business within the Tax_Exempt_Zone framework, no domestic income tax registration is required, but annual fees and license renewals are payable to SIFA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime is available under Samoa law. The tax exemption for International Companies is statutory under Section 111 of the International Companies Act 1988 (Samoa), granting full exemption from all Samoan income tax, VAGST, withholding tax, and stamp duty for a period of 20 years (renewable). ICs may elect to be treated as ordinary resident companies for domestic taxation purposes only where local-source business is undertaken, but such an election is irreversible and rarely used.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 200,000 (Samoan Tala) annual taxable turnover or likely annual turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate is currently enforced in Samoa. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices containing prescribed particulars under the VAGST Act 2006 and Tax Administration Act 2012. Returns must be filed electronically via the Ministry for Revenue online portal (monthly or quarterly depending on turnover class) with summary declaration of electronic invoicing records, but no national clearance ledger is implemented.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (a) goods physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of payment or removal to a customs controlled area; and (b) services supplied to a non-resident customer who is outside Samoa and not in Samoa at the time of supply, provided the services are not directly connected with land or goods situated in Samoa. Offshore software publishing and social casino game services sold via Apple IAP or Google Play Billing to overseas players will qualify as zero-rated supply where the recipient is non-resident, the payment originates offshore, and the services are legally and economically rendered outside Samoa. Supporting evidence must demonstrate the place of supply, export destination, and foreign exchange settlement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CUSDEC) / Samoa Export Declaration Form CED
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export movement (for goods) or digital service delivery log (for SaaS/gaming services)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank/PSP statement confirming offshore payment settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Tax Administration Act 2012 (Samoa), fraudulent zero-rating or invalid export claims attract shortfall penalties up to 150% of the VAGST payable, late-payment penalties, and statutory interest compounded from the due date. Deliberate falsification of export documentation carries criminal penalties including imprisonment up to 10 years and/or monetary fines up to 300 penalty units. The Ministry for Revenue may retrospectively claw back zero-rated claims and reassess VAGST at the standard 15% rate for a period of up to 7 years in cases of fraudulent or reckless misrepresentation. The underlying export proofs must be retained for at least 7 years; failure to maintain the prescribed documentation triggers automatic deregistration of the zero-rating benefit and assessment of full rate VAGST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a unified exchange-rate system for the current account; the Samoan Tala (WST) is not fully convertible for capital transactions. The Tax-Exempt International Company (IC) is considered a non-resident entity for exchange-control purposes and may hold, use, and remit foreign-currency proceeds through CBS-approved Foreign Currency Accounts (FCAs). Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are treated as a capital-account transaction requiring prior CBS approval under the Exchange Control Act 1976; however, an IC that has not engaged in domestic WST-denominated transactions and that maintains offshore treasury operations is generally granted approval automatically upon submission of audited financial statements and a tax-clearance certificate issued by the Samoa Ministry of Revenue. The practical hurdles include mandatory CBS Form OSI/OST declarations, per-transaction documentary review, and the absence of a fully developed offshore forward market in-country.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and Exchange Control Regulations, any exporter is required to realise the full export proceeds in foreign currency within three (3) months from the date of export and to offer those proceeds for sale to an authorized dealer (licensed Samoan commercial bank) within three (3) months of receipt. For digital publishing and simulated gaming services derived from offshore platforms (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing), the IC must file a quarterly CBS 'Foreign Currency Account Return' and apply for a standing retention waiver from the surrender obligation, on the grounds that the revenue constitutes offshore digital-service income and that no WST conversion is necessary because all suppliers and operating liabilities are settled in USD/EUR through the IC's designated FCA. In practice, CBS will approve such waivers subject to the IC maintaining separate non-resident status evidenced by the Registrar of International Companies certificate and having no local-resident trade counterparties. Without the waiver, all proceeds credited to the IC would be deemed export proceeds and would have to be converted to WST within the strict statutory timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR) in Operational / Capital Escrow Hybrid structure - dual account, non-domestic operations category

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited - BSP
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account segregated for issued share capital
Standard Corporate Operational Account (WST and USD), requiring CBS approval for FCA
Offshore deposit account under the International Companies Act - restricted investment / retained earnings account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium (legally viable with constraints). Offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex, MultiPass, and Currencycloud may serve as an ancillary settlement necklace for ad-network payables, contractor royalty payments, and subscription micro-collections; however, they are not licensed in Samoa and cannot open WST-denominated flows. The Exchange Control Act prohibits residents from routing payments through non-authorized dealers unless a CBS exemption for non-resident ICs applies. Since the target entity qualifies as a non-resident IC, it may lawfully maintain treasury relationships with foreign EMIs, but those EMIs must contractually agree to (i) avoid any Samoan resident counterparty, (ii) provide FATF-compliant sourcing evidence, and (iii) ensure that no inward or outward payment is denominated in WST. Hong Kong / Singapore EMIs with direct USD segregated settlement accounts through JP Morgan or Citibank are preferable and will materially reduce friction versus local Samoan clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement mandates that all directors appear physically before a Samoan bank. Pursuant to the AML/CFT Act 2018 and the Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Guidelines, licensed banks can perform fully remote KYC for non-resident directors via video-conferencing, provided that the directors' identity documents, passport copies, and residential proofs are notarized or apostilled and accompanied by a corporate due-diligence report from an approved international agent. For an IC engaging in simulated social casino / virtual slots publishing, the business model triggers a higher risk classification; the onboarding compliance committee will in practice require at least one physical meeting or 'recognised presence' in Apia with a senior legal counsel or a director's appearance at a remote video-escrow verification facility operated by a licensed attorney. Wait times for fully arm's-length remote opening are normally 10 to 14 weeks; adding a physical meeting in Apia shortens approval to 2 to 3 weeks and is highly recommended to secure the primary banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perception of payment treasury as a gateway for simulated wagering / gambling-related money, and the presence of Apple IAP / Google Play Billing as uncollated digital-receipt rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1. Executed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Publishing Agreement, each clearly prohibiting the payout of virtual winnings in fiat or virtual currency; 2. App-store payout statement extraction demonstrating that Apple/Google act as merchant of record and that the IC receives net-settlement remittances only; 3. Formal legal opinion from Samoan and EU target-market counsel confirming that the game qualifies as a social casino under applicable laws (no cash-out, no real-money sweepstakes); 4. A 12-month AML program narrative (SAMO_AML_POL_V1) detailing in-app item gratuity thresholds; 5. Source-of-customer-funds narrative describing Apple/Google declared payment rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious origin of initial share capital from a parent entity in a high-risk jurisdiction, combined with a low minimum-capital requirement (no statuary minimum under the IC Act).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1. Certified bank statements (last 6 months) of each founding shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO); 2. Notarized/accepted source-of-wealth declaration, and if applicable, audited parent-company financial statements; 3. Share subscription agreement with ICA-authorised director certification; 4. CBS Form AIF (Application for Inward Transfer) with an explanatory annex referencing ISIC 5820 digital-software publishing; 5. Board resolution confirming no Samoan resident beneficial ownership and no connection to sanctions-, FATF- or EU-list jurisdictions; 6. Issuance of a signed ACR-duty to notify any change in UBO within 14 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company characteristic, inferred from the IC’s absence of physical SAW (staff, assets, web) in Samoa and foreign ownership of an exempt entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1. Current International Company registration certificate issued by the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) including the registered agent name and address (required to be in Samoa); 2. Annual Return on an International Company filed within the prescribed timeframe; 3. Comprehensive operating plan demonstrating that substantive software development, cloud infrastructure, and commercial workforce reside in New Zealand / Singapore / Taiwan but that governance decisions are made in Samoa; 4. Undertaking executed by the resident registered agent for CBS communication; 5. A tax-exemption certificate from the Ministry of Revenue; 6. A treasury management mandate that names banks and clearing providers and excludes domestic Samoan trading; 7. Audited (or management-reviewed) income statement and balance sheet for the first 8 months.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant inbound injection route is as follows: (1) The disseminating shareholder bank executes a SWIFT MT103 wire with proper ISO 20022 Purpose Code. For equity capital contributions, the required purpose code is 'CAP10 - Equity/Investment in equity capital' or APER/Samoan customs, and must quote the Samoa IC treasury profile reference and the specific CBS approval file number. (2) The inbound wire must designate the IC's Foreign Currency Account (USD or EUR) at ANZ Samoa or BSP, and must include the beneficiary line as 'BENEF: WS_IC -- International Company'. (3) The remitter shall supply an Electronic Transfer Advice, together with a copy of the executed share subscription agreement, board resolution approving the issuance, and the UBO declarations; the receiving Samoan bank will file CBS Form AIF and will not credit the account until the bank's AML department sends a 'clear display notice' and the CBS auto-approval window of 2 business days has elapsed. (4) Funds exceeding WST-equivalent 1,000,000 require approval of the CBS Financial Markets Unit via a signed a pre-approval application; the routes for interim treasury funding are bank-guaranteed cheque, Swift MT101 (transfers) or MT202 (interbank transfers) from the IO's sub-account at the same bank. (5) For early-stage operations, it is advisable to structure a convertible loan facility rather than immediate equity injection; if so, the purpose code becomes 'CL02 - Intercompany Foreign Direct Investment Loans' and the contract must include an arm's-length interest rate, a maturity profile, and a licence to remit to non-resident lenders.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements are grouped into three clearing tiers: (i) payables for cloud infrastructure, IP licensing, user-acquisition advertising, and distributed developer compensation—all settled via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) to beneficiary banks worldwide, with the corresponding beneficiary's name and local bank account number, referencing invoices and the framework agreement; (ii) inter-company management fees and contractor payments where the beneficiary is outside Samoa—settled via MT103 or MT202 (for interbank cover) executed by the IC's treasury; and (iii) commercial letters of credit—legally permissible but practically inapplicable to intangible digital publishing; where required for physical merchandise (such as a distributor-created console or gift-card residue), a 'Digi-LC' arrangement can be opened through ANZ Samoa with an issuing bank outside Samoa. For Apple IAP and Google Play Billing balances, the IC will route a daily/weekly settlement sweep from the App Store merchant account into its USD concentration account through the same MT103 rail. All outbound transactions above WST100,000 must be filed with the CBS on Form OST (Overseas Settlement of Transfer) and must retain the underlying invoice / contract as the documentary audit trail. It is recommended to set a USDto-EUR conversion tolerance of 10% and to maintain an operating balance at the concentration bank in USD using internal sweep to avoid tele-transfer conversion spread.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted by the parent treasury with licensed international banks, given the Tala's non-deliverable status outside Samoa
Direct USD/EUR with forward outright contracts to hedge software licensing and contractor disbursements paid in EUR
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR) to convert long-term capital loan surplus into USD operating liquidity without driving tax-exempt `currency unrelated business` characterization
Plain vanilla foreign currency options (USD put / WST call and EUR/USD collars) for downside protection on convertible capital injections, strictly limited to 30% of the forecast WST profit clearing
Currency futures (only through shore-based exchanges such as CME) provided the regulator accepts the IC's non-resident exemption and prohibits Samoan local-market delivery

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual government license renewal (International Companies (Fees) Regulations 2008)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable each calendar year on or before the anniversary of incorporation; a late fee applies if paid after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of up to USD 50 per month or part thereof; continued non-payment for 6 months results in administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration for registered agent (confirmation of UBO register accuracy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent in Samoa; the agent is obliged to maintain and produce the UBO register to the International Companies Office or Financial Intelligence Unit upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following each anniversary of incorporation; any change of beneficial owner must be filed with the registered agent within 14 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an accurate UBO register may lead to fines up to USD 5,000 and in case of a false declaration, criminal penalties including imprisonment of up to 5 years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual certification of compliance with International Companies Act 1987 (registered agent's statutory obligation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed by the registered agent concurrently with the annual government fee payment on the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the certification is not submitted, the registrar may impose a penalty of USD 100 and, after 90 days of further non-compliance, initiate strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is not required for a standard Samoa International Company unless it is a public company, has issued securities to the public, or has consolidated assets exceeding USD 1,000,000; otherwise no statutory audit is mandated
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory accounting framework for exempt International Companies; if financial statements are prepared, International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are generally adopted for internal and financing purposes

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must update its register of beneficial owners through the registered agent. An annual confirmation of the UBO register is required on the anniversary of incorporation. Any transfer of shares during the year, resulting in a change of beneficial ownership, must be recorded in the register within 14 days and reflected in the next annual confirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,200 annually for professional registered agent and office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if exempt; voluntary audit preparation typically USD 1,500 - USD 3,000 for a small entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2012, as amended by the FY2020/21 Budget (27% prior to 1 July 2020). International Companies (IC), the target entity class, are wholly exempt from Samoa income tax by force of Section 200 of the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), producing an effective Samoan CIT burden of 0% on exempt offshore income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Total statutory tax holiday for International Companies: no CIT, no non-resident dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax on IC distributions, no capital gains tax, no stamp duty on IC instruments, and no VAT/GST on offshore revenue. Only a flat annual Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) government fee is payable (USD 500 per annum for authorized capital up to USD 1,000,000; small escalation above that threshold), plus the licensed registered agent fee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Renewal (administrative return, not a CIT return): the registered agent files the Annual Renewal / Certification of International Company (SIFA Form IC-AR) electronically through the SIFA Registry (Samoa International Finance Authority, Apia) e-portal. The IC does not file a Form TR-2 corporate income tax return with the Ministry of Revenue while it remains within the exempt zone.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (filed on, or within 180 days immediately after, the anniversary of incorporation; SIFA renewal cycle).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than the anniversary date of incorporation. The renewal fee covers the next 12-month period; a late renewal within 12 months is accepted with a surcharge, and non-renewal beyond 12 months results in automatic strike-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact registered name of the International Company and its IC registration number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the English/Chinese trade name used in the Apple App Store and Google Play developer account; notify the SIFA agent of any trading-name variation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and license number of the SIFA-licensed registered agent and the Apia registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident beneficial owner does not sign; the licensed agent certifies the office and digitally signs the renewal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital, number of issued shares, share class description and currency of account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee band is computed on authorized capital; increases of authorized capital effected by Board resolution attract a registration duty of 0.1% on the increase.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address and nationality of each director, the company secretary and (unless bearer shares are in issue) each shareholder
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The shareholders register is maintained at the registered office and is not publicly filed; only director/secretary particulars are certified in the renewal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the IC has not carried on business in Samoa with Samoan residents, has not derived Samoan-source income, and does not own Samoan land or other immovable property
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the declaration cannot be truthfully given, the IC loses statutory exemption and must file a resident/non-resident company income tax return with the Ministry of Revenue at 25%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contemporaneous statement of the class and volume of offshore business (software publishers: platform licenses, in-app purchase settlement, Apple/Google disbursements)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bank statements of settlement funding, platform payouts and IP licensing agreements should be held by the agent to evidence that all activity is outside Samoa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late renewal: surcharge for each commenced month of delay (up to 10% of the annual fee) and ultimate strike-off after 12 months of non-payment; strike-off leads to forfeiture of the IC's Samoan assets and contractual validity of the entity; restoration requires court order? (Registrar reinstatement) with a reinstatement fee plus all arrears; directors and shareholders may be disqualified from maintaining another Samoan IC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (Form TR-2) - only for an IC that has lost its exemption or an ordinary Samoan company; filed with the Ministry of Revenue (Samoa) through the e-Tax filing portal, Apia.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after balance date (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end); tax must be paid in three provisional instalments (30 June, 30 September, 31 December) plus a terminal payment at the return date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide income for a resident company; Samoa-source income only for a non-resident company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An IC with no Samoan-source receipts files a nil return and attaches the exemption notice; a non-resident IC with Samoan-source revenue is taxable only on that revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred in deriving assessable income; apportionment required for mixed use
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apple/Google commission, iPod/HTML5? platform commissions and Intercompany royalties are deductible only to the extent of arm's length and substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year losses deducted; maximum carry-forward is five years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred while the IC was taxable can be carried forward; losses incurred in the exempt period are disregarded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax computed at 25% on taxable income; tax credits for Samoan WHT/foreign tax are then applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax credits arise on Samoan-source interest/royalties; unilateral foreign tax credits are not available (treaty credits only).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of cross-border related-party transactions and TP methodology applied (CUP, resale, cost-plus, TNMM, profit split)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete for all intercompany royalties for the game IP and platform settlement arrangements; attach the Local File summary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of up to 20% of the tax returnable, late payment interest at the statutory monthly rate (2% per month), and imprisonment up to two years for willful non-filing; the Commissioner may raise a default assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for an exempt International Company: distributions of profits to non-resident shareholders are made free of any Samoan dividend withholding tax because the IC is wholly outside the Income Tax Act 2012. By contrast, a resident company under the Income Tax Act 2012 pays a final dividend withholding tax of 15% on gross distributions to non-resident shareholders (the IC exemption therefore acts as an incentive for the family-trust holding structure).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For IC distributions, no treaty relief application is needed in Samoa since the source-state WHT is nil. If the IC pays or receives royalties/interest from a treaty partner (e.g., China, under the Samoa-China DTA in force since 2015), the beneficial owner must obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate from the Ministry of Revenue (Form TRC), submit it with a beneficial-ownership declaration to the payer before the payment is made, and, where required by the source state, file the prescribed treaty-relief form (e.g., the Chinese non-resident treaty-benefit form) so that the payer may apply the reduced rate at source; the relief is claim-based and not automatic.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoan WHT on royalties and interest paid to non-residents: 15% each (final WHT). Treaty-reduced rates: Samoa-China DTA - interest 10%, royalties 10%, dividends 5% (company holding at least 10% of capital) / 15% (otherwise); Samoa-Australia DTA and Samoa-New Zealand DTA follow similar accordance: interest 10%, royalties 10%, dividends 5%/15% (per treaty text). For an exempt IC paying no Samoan tax, the practical WHT exposure arises in the residence-state of the payer (e.g., Ireland/US on Apple/Google settlement) and is governed by the payer's domestic law and the relevant DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Samoa threshold (in WST) triggers Local File/Master File compilation; the Income Tax Act 2012 imposes the arm's length standard on all cross-border related-party transactions and the Commissioner may require contemporaneous TP documentation on demand (within 30 days). A prudent IC holding game IP should nonetheless prepare an OECD-aligned Local File when annual related-party flows exceed WST 2,000,000 (approx USD 700,000) to withstand audit, even though no TP filing is made in the exempt zone; China-side documentation thresholds (e.g., related-party transactions over RMB 100 million under Chinese SAT rules) must be separately observed by the Chinese beneficial owner.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP - comparable uncontrolled price (particularly for platform commissions)
Resale price method (applicable to distribution of virtual tokens through IAP if reseller functions exist)
Cost-plus method (margin on development services rendered to the IC)
TNMM - transactional net margin method (preferred for the IC's licensing/settlement functions)
Profit split method (for integrated China-development + Samoa-IP arrangements)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to BVI/Cayman ESR; the IC regime relies on statutory ring-fencing: the International Companies Act 1987 prohibits the IC from carrying on business with Samoan residents, deriving Samoan-source income or owning Samoan land, and requires a licensed Apia registered agent, registered office and resident secretary. The OECD FHTP (BEPS Inclusive Framework) monitors Samoa's status; an IC should maintain board minutes, bank records and IP license agreements in Samoa and perform genuinely strategic functions (execution of board decisions, approval of IP sub-licenses, distribution resolutions) to establish substance and defuse DTA/GAAR challenges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false exempt-status declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring the IC to be 'wholly exempt' while deliberately concealing Samoan-source revenue or business with Samoan residents (e.g., hiring local employees to serve the Samoan market or collecting local merchant income), or knowingly understating the Samoan content of app-store revenue in the e-Tax return once exemption lapses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2012 and Tax Administration Act 2012: penalty of 150% of the evaded tax plus default interest of 2% per month, administrative fine up to WST 100,000, and the Commissioner's power to estimate and garnish bank accounts at the Samoan settlement bank.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certified a false Box 5 declaration are personally and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax; conviction carries imprisonment up to five years, director disqualification and a summary travel restriction: the Ministry of Revenue may issue a departure prohibition certificate preventing the director from leaving Samoa until the assessed tax and penalty are secured.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-company / sham substance and corporate veil piercing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC as a paper entity without a functioning registered agent, with fabricated director/shareholder records or bearer-style nominee arrangements, or using the IC solely as a billing and IP conduit while all strategic decisions occur in China without formal license, board or treasury records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registrar of International Companies may strike off the company and forfeit its assets after 12 months of non-renewal; on strike-off, all contracts (including Apple/Google developer agreements) are legally terminated, the IC is dissolved, and assets are vested in the Registrar; restoration requires a reinstatement fee and court approval in contested cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Samoan courts will pierce the corporate veil: controlling shareholders and shadow directors are jointly liable for the company's debts, restitution of platform proceeds is ordered to affected parties and the Crown, and directors may be banned from incorporating or administering any Samoan entity for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing social-casino in-app purchase settlements and virtual-currency transaction flows through the IC without a Samoan AML/CFT program, accepting round-trip third-party funding or use of unverified prepaid/offshore cards, failing to maintain beneficial-ownership records (including the ultimate Chinese trust settlor), or transacting with sanctioned jurisdictions/counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018 (Samoa): corporate fines up to WST 2,000,000, confiscation of proceeds under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2007, and the Financial Intelligence Unit's power to freeze the IC's bank accounts and tipping-off penalties for the registered agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and beneficial owners are subject to criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 14 years for money laundering (and up to 7 years for financing of terrorism), personal asset forfeiture, international extradition to the requesting state, and cross-border travel bans issued at the request of the FIU or foreign enforcement authorities (e.g., the Australian/American authorities under the FATF network).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Marketing the 'simulated social casino and virtual slots' product as a real-money wagering service, permitting unrestricted secondary-market trading of virtual chips or cash-out through third-party exchanges, or geo-routing the service to jurisdictions that regulate gambling without a licenced gaming licence - conduct that converts the exempt software-publishing IC into an unlawful Samoan and cross-border gambling operator.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Gambling Act 2008 (Samoa) only a sole Concessionaire may provide casino-style gaming in Samoa: an unauthorized IC faces fines up to WST 500,000 per offence, forfeiture of gaming equipment and platform assets, and shutdown orders; foreign regulators (e.g., UKGC, AGCO, Swedish SGA) may impose cumulative fines and block the app stores, while Apple and Google enforce clause-level termination of the developer account for unlawful gambling content.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability for operating unlawful gambling, personal fines, repatriation orders for funds received, travel bans from the licensing state, and extradition under mutual-assistance treaties; the family-trust settlor is exposed to clawback of distributed assets in the jurisdiction of the principal regulator.
